requirement: Parse order states from wire strings case-insensitively with a clear error for unknown values, enforce allowed state transitions, and parse comma-separated permission names into a combinable flag.
skeleton: OrderState Enum with a parse classmethod and a transition table, a Permission Flag with an ADMIN alias, and parse_permissions building a flag from names.
caption: Standard-library enums that turn wire strings into typed values and fail loudly on anything unknown. OrderState is an Enum whose members PENDING, PAID, SHIPPED and CANCELLED carry lower-case string values. Its classmethod parse strips and lower-cases the raw text and looks it up by value, turning the ValueError from an unknown value into a new ValueError that names the raw text as an unknown order state, chained from the original. can_transition_to(target) checks a module-level TRANSITIONS dictionary of frozensets: pending may become paid or cancelled, paid may become shipped or cancelled, and shipped and cancelled are terminal. Permission is a Flag with READ, WRITE and DELETE created by auto and an ADMIN member combining all three. parse_permissions(spec) starts from Permission(0), splits the text on commas, strips and upper-cases each part, skips empty parts so a trailing comma or blank text is harmless, raises ValueError naming an unknown permission when a name is not in Permission.__members__, and ors each member into the result. The fixture asserts that " PAID " parses to PAID, that refunded raises ValueError with a ValueError cause, that pending may become paid but paid may not return to pending and shipped may not be cancelled, that "read, write," yields READ and WRITE without DELETE while admin includes DELETE, that empty and blank specs grant nothing, and that execute raises ValueError naming EXECUTE.

plan.intent: Parse order states and permissions from wire text into enums
constraints: State parsing ignores case and surrounding spaces
An unknown state raises ValueError chained from the lookup error
Shipped and cancelled orders cannot transition anywhere
Permission names are comma separated, empty parts are skipped, and an unknown name raises ValueError
An empty spec yields no permissions

rationale.teaches: Enum lookup by value with a domain error, a transition table keyed by members, and Flag composition from parsed names.
rationale.why: Enum lookups fail with KeyError by name and ValueError by value, and a Flag parsed from text silently grants a default when it starts from the wrong value. Parsing real wire strings at the edges shows which lookup and which starting value the code uses.

ops.docstring: Parse order states and permission flags from wire strings with explicit failures.

ops.stmt: from enum import Enum, Flag, auto

ops.source:
class Permission(Flag):
    """Permissions that combine into one value."""

    READ = auto()
    WRITE = auto()
    DELETE = auto()
    ADMIN = READ | WRITE | DELETE

candidates.why_wrong: An unknown permission name escapes as a bare KeyError instead of a ValueError naming it.
States are looked up by member name, so an unknown value raises KeyError and is never reported as an unknown order state.
A shipped order may still be cancelled.
Parsing starts from READ, so an empty spec still grants read access.
Empty parts are not skipped, so a trailing comma or a blank spec is rejected as an unknown permission.
